title: Replying to @Nico Juber another thing Starkid consistently does bette...
transcript: Why aren't we getting full cast albums anymore? The answer, of course, is money. We know the answer is money, but a little piece of me is like, well, what can we do to counteract that? Right? And Nico brought up a good point in her reply to this comment that we don't buy physical media like we used to in the 90s and 2. And so it's harder for people, after they raise money for cast albums to make money off of the cast album. Because artists don't make money off of streaming. Right? They make money from selling physical media. But then I look at the Taylor Swift of it all and the fact that she is an artist is able to sell multiple variants of the same album. And yet Broadway hasn't figured out how to capitalize off of the resurgence of physical media. I don't even like this ragtime revival, but if they released a full edition that was physical media only that included all of the scenic transitions and Atlantic City, I would buy that so fast. Makes me wonder, how much did Andrew Lloyd Weber and company make off of the multiple Sunset Boulevard variants that were like near $100 each? There is a resurgence for this love of physical media. And if you give people something that they can only get in the physical media that they cannot stream, then you can have the truncated version on streaming that people can add all their Favourite songs to the playlist. And then for the people who are going to sit down and listen to the full album, offer the physical media that you then make money off of. And I don't know the financials, I don't know how much money you would realistically make. And I don't think that this is the right choice for say, a brand new concept album or a studio cast recording or an off Broadway show that is like really scraping pennies together. But when you have a hit Broadway show that we are getting like a, a complete cast recording for completionist sake, there's going to be fans at that point who are going to purchase the full thing. It's no longer necessarily a marketing tool. It is now become a. An archival piece of history. And so I do think that there's a difference. And especially for big Broadway productions, and especially as we start getting revivals of like shows that we don't have complete cast albums of, then I do think that there's value in that and that fans would purchase that and that that could be a money making income. However, at the end of the day, I'm always going to be frustrated about the fact that because of this really capitalist society that we live in, that we have to talk about archiving art this way. Because everything always comes back to money. And I just. Aggggh! I hate it. I hate it.
classificationReason: Industry commentary about physical media and cast albums; briefly mentions Ragtime and Sunset Boulevard but doesn't review either. No single show focus — general industry discussion.
